title: Conrad Flynn: backgrounder
summary: Conrad Flynn is a Los Angeles writer, producer and podcaster who writes about the "secret histories" of Hollywood, rock music and the occult. In October 2025 he spent an episode of The Tucker Carlson Show presenting Nick Land as a hidden influence on Silicon Valley's AI culture, which made Land a topic on the American right. On 31 October 2026 he and Land spoke for the first time, on The Dangerous Maybe.

p: Flynn describes himself as a writer and producer in Los Angeles and a former stand-up comic. His main outlets are a Substack newsletter, The Flynn Effect (more than 5,000 subscribers, per Substack), an Instagram account on mainstream Hollywood history, and a podcast he says is launching soon.

By his own account on Tucker Carlson's show, his grandfathers were the actor Robert Conrad, star of The Wild Wild West, and the Hollywood publicist Harry Flynn. This desk found no independent source for the family details, so treat them as his claim.

He says his interest in Land grew out of research for "Running with the Devil," a planned project on rock music and the occult. He names as collaborators the critics Stephen Thomas Erlewine and Ned Raggett, and Sue Kolinsky and Greg Johnston, whom he credits with creating The Osbournes. The project shows up in his Substack (for example, a 28 April 2026 essay on Kate Bush and the occult, written with Erlewine). The collaborator list is unconfirmed beyond his own statements.

The episode was titled "The Occult, Kabbalah, the Antichrist's Newest Manifestation, and How to Avoid the Mark of the Beast." A transcript index dates it to 3 October 2025. Flynn called Land "the Timothy Leary of the 90s," held up CCRU's Numogram on air, explained its "lemurs" as spirits, and claimed that tech insiders read Land's occult side as well as his philosophy. He also floated blockchain as a possible "mark of the beast" and warned about AI in biblical terms.

The interview spread widely. Critics on X complained that Carlson pushed back on almost none of it. In Compact magazine on 15 October 2025, Geoff Shullenberger summarized Flynn's claims. He quoted Land as saying he had "no idea" how much influence he has in Silicon Valley, and calling Flynn a "master of narrative." Land answered at length in a response video with The Dangerous Maybe hosts a few days after the episode.

sources.label: Compact: "The Faith of Nick Land" (Geoff Shullenberger, 15 Oct 2025)

p: Flynn has been on Billy Corgan's podcast The Magnificent Others at least three times. He has also been on Jack Osbourne's podcast Trying Not to Die, in an episode titled "What Hollywood Doesn't Want You to Notice." His Substack runs guest pieces and follow-ups, including one pointing Tucker listeners to the historian Rick Spence.

sources.label: Trying Not to Die with Jack Osbourne

p: The Dangerous Maybe released a 3-hour-17-minute Halloween conversation between Flynn and Land, hosted by Mikey Downs and Nance, billed as "over a year in the making." Flynn's style there matches his Tucker appearance: long chains of connections (Aphex Twin to the CCRU website, Interstellar's tesseract to Charles and Geoffrey Hinton, Musk's grandfather to the Technocracy movement), many of them interesting and some of them unverified.

At the end, Flynn says a Carlson producer had asked him that week for Land's contact details, and that Carlson's team plans to be in Shanghai in November. Land agreed on air to do the interview. Only Flynn's account supports this so far.

p: No independent source found by this desk confirms Flynn's family links to Robert Conrad and Harry Flynn, the full list of his rock-and-occult collaborators, or the Carlson producer's request. This desk did not find a verified X account for him. Do not confuse him with other people named Flynn, such as Michael Flynn (@GenFlynn).
